Scores are 1-5 and unvalidated: importance = historical weight of what the text could add; solvability = odds of a full reading with the material available online; difficulty = technical work needed (1 trivial key alignment, 5 statistics-only on an unknown system). Priority is computed on the page from adjustable weights. Class A = siblings with decipherment in the same volume, B = partial key or known family in print, C = no key, no sibling. seen: image = leaf viewed on the Gallica image; catalogue = selected from the catalogue description only. outcome: 'attempted, open' once an entry has been taken to the leaf here without a reading. Entries read, partly read, resolved or found already in print are removed from this file (19 Sept 2026) and recorded in SOLVED_CATALOGUE.md; ids are not reused. contributed_by: the contributors.json id of an outside contributor who brought the entry in (shown on the page as 'via ...').

entries.title: Hieronimo Ranzo (?) to 'Garbino', intercepted imperial letter
entries.correspondents: Hieronimo Ranzo (probably; Gattinara's man) → 'Garbino'
entries.shelfmark: BnF fr. 3022 no. 20 (ff. 44r–46v; addition sheet and jargon ff. 48–50v)
entries.status: The other two items first catalogued here (nos. 6 and 10, del Vasto to Charles V) are read: no. 10 by Lasry (2023) with Tomokiyo's edited text, no. 6 in targets/vasto1527/ (its own page since 14 Oct 2026). No. 20 is an Italian letter, Madrid 11 Apr 1528, to 'Garbino', in the same code as Hieronimo Ranzo's letters (fr. 2988). The key was recovered from the ciphertext by George Lasry and, independently, by Paolo Rosson (6 Oct 2026; PRs #35, #45), and no. 20 measures 94.4% (targets/ranzo1528/, 18 Oct 2026), just under the read bar. entries.title: Florence, letters to the Signoria in the cipher of 1414 (Gabbrielli's partial key, letters never read)
entries.correspondents: unknown Florentine envoy or commissary → Signoria / Dieci di Balìa
entries.shelfmark: ASF, Signori, Responsive originali, filza 1 (key: ASF Chiavi delle cifre II, pars 3 no. 1)
entries.status: Meister 1902 p. 49 prints "Florenz, Beispiele 1: Cifra Decemviri di Balia 1414 (Lettere della Signoria risponsive; filza Nr. 1)", a partial homophonic alphabet Gabbrielli rebuilt in 1864 from glossed words (several letters blank; per = 8, et = f, che = dum). No sender or folio given; no reading of the letters printed (Guasti's Commissioni has nothing for 1414). The same situation as florence1429, where Gabbrielli's 1424 table read only glossed words. Session of 23 Sept 2026 (targets/florence1414/): key transcribed (KEY.md, 38 signs); 'filza 1' is an old number (today's Signori Responsive 1 is 1340), so the letters are probably in Signori Responsive 7-8 or Signori-Dieci-Otto, Legazioni e commissarie, missive e responsive 8; not on DECODE, Yale Ilardi reels or ASF PAD. Outgoing registers Legazioni e commissarie 5-6 (PAD) scanned: clear, no cipher; reg. 6 ff. ~35-52 are the 1414 instructions (candidate senders).
entries.why: The oldest Florentine cipher letters; a full reading would beat the project's 1425 record by eleven years.
entries.verify: Order from ASF: Gabbrielli vol. II pars 3 no. 1 (key page with his list of letters used) and the vol. II index, then the letters (likely Signori Responsive 7-8 or Legazioni e commissarie, missive e responsive 8). Then read as in florence1429.
entries.outcome: attempted, open: blocked, no image of the letters online (23 Sept 2026, targets/florence1414/)
entries.known: Gabbrielli's 1864 partial key (printed by Meister 1902, p. 49) transcribed here as 38 signs (florence1414). No reading of any of the letters has been found.
entries.open: The 1414 letters themselves: not located or imaged (probably ASF Signori Responsive 7-8 or Legazioni e commissarie 8); not on DECODE, Ilardi reels or ASF PAD. Blocker: needs ASF photographs.

entries.title: Siena, "Lettere in cifra" of the Concistoro: the pieces still unsolved (nos. 7, 19, 21; no. 1 of 1421 unphotographed)
entries.correspondents: Sienese envoys and others → the Concistoro of Siena
entries.shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Siena, Concistoro 2308, fasc. 2 "Lettere in cifra": nos. 7, 19, 21 (R4796, R4807, R4809); no. 1 (1421), 2, 26-28 (not on DECODE)
entries.status: Narrowed 18 Oct 2026 to the pieces still unsolved, after George Lasry's report of 17 Oct 2026 (one entry per key; index research/siena2308/). Open: no. 7 (R4796, orator at Milan to the Balia, 1450s; 363 signs, interlinear gloss gives nine values; filed key R4750 and five others fail it; targets/siena7/), no. 19 (R4807, Sienese envoys, 9 March, 1440s; 118 signs; targets/siena19/), no. 21 (R4809, 'Karissimo come padre', 15th c.; 107 signs; targets/siena21/): attempted, too short without a key. No. 1 (1421) and nos. 2, 26-28 are not among the DECODE photographs (needs ASSi). The other pieces are deciphered on their own entries: nos. 20/23, 12, 6/24, 4, 14, 25, 11, 18, 17, 15, 5?, 9, 13/16, 10 and 8 (no. 8 from the contemporary decipherment on its sheet, aligned here 18 Oct 2026).
entries.why: Nos. 7, 19 and 21 are the last undeciphered 15th-century pieces of the Sienese file. No. 1 (1421) would not be its oldest letter: George Lasry's decipherments include letters of March and April 1413 (nos. 12, 20, 23; the years reconstructed, not written).
entries.verify: Order nos. 1, 2, 26-28 from ASSi; for nos. 7, 19, 21 look for a sibling letter in the same key or a fresh transcription in CTTS (no. 7: rerun with the gloss values fixed).
entries.known: Every other photographed piece is deciphered on its own entry (index: siena1421.html). George Lasry recovered the keys of no. 12, 10 March 1413 (the year reconstructed from the sixth indiction and the context), nos. 20 and 23, 30 March and about April 1413 (years inferred), nos. 6/24, 9, 11, 13/16, 17, R4794 and no. 15 in part; this project recovered nos. 4, 18, 25 and no. 14 in part; nos. 8 and 10 were deciphered at the time. No. 7: the interlinear gloss gives nine values.
entries.open: Nos. 7 (R4796, 363 signs), 19 (R4807, 118) and 21 (R4809, 107): no key; none of the filed keys fits, and neither George Lasry nor this project has deciphered them. No. 1 (Meister's 1421 letter), 2 and 26-28 are not photographed; they need the Archivio di Stato di Siena.

entries.title: Military news for Prince Carl August Friedrich of Waldeck, in a three-digit code
entries.correspondents: unknown informant → Prince Carl August Friedrich of Waldeck
entries.shelfmark: Hessisches Staatsarchiv Marburg, HStAM 118 a Nr. 3954, ff. 3-4 (HCPortal record 517)
entries.status: Attempted 28 Sept 2026 (targets/waldeck1744/): 717 groups, 303 distinct, transcribed. The prince's French draft reply on f. 4v answers a letter of 18 January (1744). Probably a two-part homophonic nomenclator (7/90/924 homophones; no alphabetical, column or multiplicative numbering fits); synthetic controls of that design show the key is not identifiable from one letter. No key on Arcinsys, HCPortal or DECODE; the undigitised 118 a Nr. 1973-1980 (Feldzug 1744) may hold the key or a deciphered copy.
entries.why: War of the Austrian Succession; Waldeck commanded Dutch troops. A hard code with no known key.
entries.verify: Look for further reports in the same code in HStAM 118 a (Waldeck papers) before attempting; one page of code is thin.
entries.known: Nothing deciphered. 717 groups transcribed 28 Sept 2026; dated 18 Jan 1744 from the prince's draft reply on f. 4v (waldeck1744).
entries.open: The whole letter: not deciphered. Two-part nomenclator with no key on Arcinsys, HCPortal or DECODE; synthetic controls show one letter is too little to rebuild it; possible key or copy in undigitised HStAM 118 a Nr. 1973-1980.
